text: Keep your hands off the anvil unless you want broken fingers.
Good steel does not whine when the hammer strikes it.
If you break that blade, do not come crying to my forge.
Cold iron bends for no one without honest sweat and heavy fire.
Buy something useful or stop blocking the bellows.
A dull sword is worse than an empty sheath, lad.
I forge weapons to kill beasts, not for strutting around market squares.
Pay the coin first, inspect the crossguard second.
The fire needs more coal if we want tempered bronze.
Tough armor will not save a fool who forgets how to dodge.
Hammer and anvil teach lessons that words never could.
Do not swing that hammer like a broom stick.
Iron remembers every strike of the master.
Stand clear of the sparks or nurse your burns alone.
A heavy shield takes time and raw muscle to shape.
I have been pounding red hot iron since before you could walk.
The tongs are hot, so back away from the furnace.
True craft requires grease, grit, and stubborn pride.
You want a masterpiece, but you brought pocket copper.
The forge will not wait while you daydream.
Sharpen that edge before the rust eats your dinner.
A blacksmith does not bargain with fools who break tools.
Put some weight behind your arm or put down the mallet.
Steel sings when quenched right, and screeches when rushed.
Shut the workshop door; the draft ruins the furnace heat.
A warrior who respects his weapon cleans the pommel every night.
The stars align in fractured geometries above the weeping spire.
Whispers in the ether reveal what mortal eyes refuse to witness.
Ancient runes remember the oaths forgotten by mortal blood.
Magic is not commanded; it is woven through quiet patience.
Every shadow cast by moonlight carries an unspoken secret.
The celestial veil thins when the silver comet awakens.
Disturb not the ley lines unless you welcome an arcane storm.
Time bends like silk beneath the weight of prophecy.
Listen closely, traveler, for the stones speak in riddles.
The arcane glyphs pulse with ancient slumbering power.
A circle drawn in ash can hold back forgotten horrors.
Look into the scrying glass and see what tomorrow conceals.
The astral winds whisper names that were never spoken aloud.
Knowledge is a fire that consumes the vessel holding it.
Do not touch the crystal orb while the eclipse remains unbroken.
The cosmos remembers what kings choose to forget.
Between two heartbeats lies the doorway to the Nether Realm.
The stars speak only when mortals cease their clamor.
We are merely shadows walking across an ancient parchment.
Speak the secret incantation only when the twin moons cross.
Every spell leaves an invisible ripple across the astral tide.
Beware the silence of the void, for it listens hungry.
The runes glow blue when destiny turns its wheel.
Fate is an intricate tapestry woven with silver threads.
You seek answers, yet you fear the light that brings them.
The ethereal plane shifts with every breath of the cosmos.
A song in the tavern brings brighter dawn than golden crowns!
Raise your tankards high and let the merry lute sing!
Every dragon has a tale, and every hero needs a ballad!
A smile costs no silver, but a good tune buys warm cider!
Dance upon the cobblestones while the fiddle plays sweet tunes!
Life is a joyous carnival for those bold enough to laugh!
Gather round, brave folk, and hear the ballad of the golden feather!
No monster is too terrifying when met with jolly courage and verse!
Sing with me under the lanterns until the morning sun rises!
A hearty laugh scatters dark clouds faster than any spell!
Another round of spiced ale for the grand storytellers!
Strum the strings, tap your boots, and shake away all sorrow!
A traveler without a song is like a bird without wings!
The prettiest melodies are found where good friends gather.
Give me a rhyming verse and I will charm the grumpiest guard!
Even fierce knights smile when the flute plays the village reel!
What is glory without a ballad to keep your legend alive?
Let your heart leap like a trout in a sunlit stream!
There is magic in laughter that philosophers could never write down!
Fill my cap with coppers and I shall sing until midnight!
Raise your voices, my companions, the road ahead is bright!
A sunny day and a jolly rhyme can cure any broken spirit!
The tavern fire is warm and the ballad has only just begun!
Come now, clap your hands and toast to friendship!
Adventure awaits just beyond the festival gates!
Sweet wine and merry harmonies make every evening worthwhile!
Step softly, or your next footprint will be your last.
Shadows are kinder allies than honest promises in this city.
A quick dagger solves puzzles that philosophers argue about for years.
Watch your coin pouch, or someone lighter on their feet will.
The night has ears, and the alleyways keep no promises.
Never look a smuggler in the eyes before checking the exits.
Quiet blades leave no witness to tell tales to the watch.
Gold talks louder than courage when the tavern lanterns dim.
Trust is a luxury only the dead can afford out here.
One wrong turn in the sewer maze and you feed the wharf rats.
Keep your back against the brick and your fingers near your blade.
A locked door is merely an invitation written in iron.
The city watch is slow, but arrows fly faster than apologies.
Never carry more loot than you can run with over rooftops.
Poison on the dart is subtle, silent, and wonderfully persuasive.
If anyone asks, we were never drinking at this corner.
Rooftops belong to crows, cats, and those who avoid city taxes.
A slipped knot and a greased hinge make quick escapes easy.
Do not whisper secrets when the cobblestones are wet with rain.
Every lock has a weakness if you know which pick to turn.
Gold in hand is better than promises signed by corrupt nobles.
Stay in the shadows until the torchbearer passes your perch.
A good thief knows when to pocket the loot and vanish.
Curiosity gets common folk killed in these winding alleys.
Keep your voice low; walls have cracks and beggars have ears.
A cloak of dark wool hides more blood than silk ever will.
